name: Sioux Falls
tagline: No State Income Tax, Ultra-Low Costs, and Falls Park Beauty
description: Sioux Falls is a FIRE powerhouse hiding in plain sight. South Dakota has zero state income tax, and the cost of living here is among the lowest in the nation. The city is anchored by the stunning Falls Park, a revitalized downtown with craft breweries and local restaurants, and an increasingly vibrant cultural scene. With a growing population, excellent healthcare at Sanford and Avera, and endless outdoor recreation along the Big Sioux River, this is one of the smartest places in America to stretch your FIRE portfolio.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – one of the safest cities in the Upper Midwest
quickFacts.climate: Continental with cold, snowy winters and warm, humid summers

housing.description: Frugal studio or small older 1BR in the Cathedral District or near Falls Park (studio avg ~$700–873; 1BR ~$900–972)

healthcare.description: A subsidized ACA Silver plan, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600; the subsidized cost is capped by income and fairly similar across states, but above the cutoff it climbs into South Dakota's unsubsidized range. Priced for ages 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off economy car (Sioux Falls insurance is low ~$112/mo liability) plus fuel and upkeep

entertainment.description: Falls Park, Big Sioux River trails, SculptureWalk, free community events

1M.lifestyle: A frugal studio or small older one-bedroom in the Cathedral District or near Falls Park anchors a modest but genuinely comfortable baseline, helped by South Dakota's zero state income tax. Cooking at home is the norm, a paid-off car handles the errands that light transit cannot, and healthcare rests on a subsidized Silver plan tied to keeping income under the ACA cliff. Evenings and weekends revolve around Falls Park, the Big Sioux River trails, and SculptureWalk. Housing plus the health premium are the two big lines, but the low cost base leaves real breathing room.

housing.description: A nice 1BR in McKennan Park or the Cathedral District

healthcare.description: Subsidized / near-benchmark Silver at mid-range income

transportation.description: A newer used car, full coverage (~$154/mo), plus fuel and upkeep

2M.lifestyle: A nice one-bedroom in a tree-lined neighborhood like McKennan Park, eating out a few times a week, and a newer used car on full coverage for the winters. Health coverage is a subsidized or near-benchmark Silver plan, and there is comfortable room for the Washington Pavilion, a gym, and hobbies. The low cost base and zero state income tax leave a healthy monthly margin.

housing.description: A premium 1BR or small 2BR in a top building near Lake Lorraine, The Bluffs, or luxury downtown

healthcare.description: Cliff-edge and padded; the swing variable — a drawdown can push MAGI over the ~$62,600 cliff into SD's full unsubsidized band (an age-45–55 adult jumps toward ~$950–1,180 unsubsidized Silver)

transportation.description: A reliable late-model car, premium full coverage, fuel and upkeep

entertainment.description: Denny Sanford Premier Center events, clubs, travel-lite

3M.lifestyle: A relaxed, financially-independent life in a premium apartment near Lake Lorraine or The Bluffs, dining out several times a week with a genuine travel budget. A reliable late-model car handles Dakota winters, and there is room for Premier Center events, clubs, and hobbies. Healthcare is the swing variable — the line is padded because a drawdown can push income over the ACA cliff into South Dakota's full unsubsidized band. Everything is covered comfortably; the only real constraint is discretionary scale, not comfort.

housing.description: A luxury 2BR or upscale rental in The Bluffs or the Lake Lorraine area

healthcare.description: A fully unsubsidized low-deductible Gold plan, age-rated for a 45–55 adult (SD's moderate benchmark keeps this mid-band, below Nebraska-style highs)

transportation.description: A nice newer vehicle, premium coverage, all-in

luxuryExtras.description: A travel fund, club memberships, wine, premium services

5M.lifestyle: A luxury apartment or upscale rental in The Bluffs or the Lake Lorraine area, frequent fine dining, and a nice newer vehicle. Health coverage is a fully unsubsidized low-deductible Gold plan, biweekly housekeeping frees up time, and a standing travel-and-experiences budget makes getaways routine. Zero state income tax means more of every withdrawal is kept — affluent living in a low-cost city.

housing.description: A top-end luxury condo, penthouse, or large luxury home rental in The Bluffs / Lake Lorraine (a conservative anchor — real penthouse stock, The Cascade at The Steel District, reaches $5,389/mo long-term; see confidence)

dining.description: Routine fine dining, chef's tables, private events

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized domestic plan plus concierge / direct-primary-care (US-domestic, not expat); SD's moderate benchmark, age-rated for a 45–55 adult, places this above ND/MI but below Nebraska

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle, full coverage, plus on-demand car service

domesticHelp.description: Weekly-plus housekeeping including grounds, snow removal, and errand support

luxuryExtras.description: Extensive travel, personal services, club memberships, luxury goods

10M.lifestyle: The top of what Sioux Falls offers — a luxury condo, penthouse, or large home in The Bluffs or Lake Lorraine, routine fine dining, and a luxury vehicle with on-demand service. Full household help keeps everything effortless, and concierge medicine sits atop a top-tier unsubsidized domestic plan. An expansive travel-and-memberships budget rounds out a well-staffed, status-comfortable life, with the state's zero income tax stretching every dollar further.
